F31 is fixed at records 140 and 141. It is the last of the fifth review's findings, and all
five are now closed.

## Verified, including a check of mine that was wrong

The assertion bites: reverting `messages.external_message_id` to its old comment, "Not buyer
PII. The rail's own id for the message", makes the suite exit 1 and name it. The database was
reset afterwards and the suite is green at 107.

One check of mine was badly built and is recorded because it nearly produced a false report.
I grepped both comments for the phrase "assigned by the rail" and flagged
`message_threads.external_thread_id` as still carrying the false claim. It does carry those
words, correctly: the comment now says the id is "assigned by the rail and chosen by nobody"
**on the four marketplace rails**, and then says mail has no such id. The claim was scoped
rather than deleted, which is the right fix because it is true on four of five rails. A
pattern match cannot tell a scoped claim from an unscoped one, which is close to the defect
F31 is about.

## The decision, and why it is the right one

The round chose a constraint on the writer over reclassifying both columns as buyer PII, and
argued it in the column's own comment rather than asserting it. The argument holds:

- One column serves both rails, so marking it PII expires marketplace thread ids that hold
  nothing about anybody, to buy nothing on those rails.
- Expiry is the wrong instrument even on mail. This id is what makes re-ingest idempotent, so
  clearing it at 30 days turns every older thread into a new thread on the next sync and the
  record grows a duplicate per thread per sync. That is worse than the defect.
- CLAUDE.md keeps buyer data only as far as a claim needs it. A claim needs to know two
  messages are one message, not which provider the buyer uses. A digest gives the first and
  carries neither host nor local part, so the data is never written rather than written and
  deleted thirty days later.

It is the device part 7 already uses for `audit_events.payload` and `claim_events.detail`, so
it is the file's own shape rather than a new one invented to avoid work.

## What it costs, which the comment states rather than hides

Prevention with no detection. A digest and a raw Message-ID are both opaque text and nothing
in this schema can tell them apart. A check constraint would fix a digest format SEEN-062 has
not chosen and would reject rows at ingest, which part 2 refused as a principle. So the
promise lives in a column comment and in `CONSTRAINED_NOT_BUYER_PII_COLUMNS`, and the new
assertion keeps the promise stated and owned rather than keeping it true.

## The twin, and the lesson repeating

F31 named `message_threads.external_thread_id` alone. `messages.external_message_id` two lines
away carried the same claim and is worse, because every inbound mail message has a Message-ID
its sender generated, not just a thread root. Both are fixed.

That is the second time on this ticket that a finding's twin sat in the next sentence: F24 was
F22's twin and survived a round because only the named sentence was fixed. Reading the
neighbours of a finding is now worth more here than reading the finding again.

## Open, and not this round's

- **The obligation binds a ticket that does not exist yet.** SEEN-062's ticket file says
  nothing about Message-ID handling. This round owns part 7 and not another ticket's criteria,
  so it did not edit it, which is right. Somebody should carry the digest obligation into
  SEEN-062's acceptance criteria before it is worked, or the only places the promise lives are
  a column comment and a list in `tables.ts`, and neither is read when a ticket is planned.
- F26 remains open and belongs to whoever owns the harness fix.

All of F19 to F25 and F27 to F31 are closed. Criterion 2 stays unticked until a review says
the evidence carries it.
